# ultra-documents
English | 中文
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ultra-documents) [](https://github.com/Libraqg/ultra-documents/acti
ons/workflows/test.yml) [](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/libraqg/ultra-documents) [](https://github
.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)
Artifacts-like documents for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).
**Get documents you can comment on, hand back to the AI for the next version, and edit yourself, rig
ht in the dsh sidebar.**

Ask the agent for a report, proposal, explainer, slide deck, diagram or
dashboard. It writes one sel

f-contained HTML page, which shows up in the chat
as a card and opens in the dsh right sidebar. Then

-contained HTML page, which shows up in the chat
as a card and opens in the dsh right sidebar. Then:

- **Comment** — select any text, or click a figure or table, and leave a
comment.
- **Send to AI** —

one click hands the open comments to the agent, which
writes the next version and answers each comm

dit** — change the text and formatting of the latest version yourself;
saving creates a new version.

Every change is a new version, and you can switch between them. Everything
stays on your machine: no
account, no server, no sharing.

In the desktop app, add the plugin from its plugin manager instead; the
desktop profile is managed b

ktop app, add the plugin from its plugin manager instead; the
desktop profile is managed by the app.
## Use

1. Start a new session in a workspace and ask for a document, for example
"Use ultra-documents to ma

ke a two-day Hangzhou itinerary with a schedule
table".
2. Click the card in the chat to open the do

witch to read mode to interact with the page normally.
4. Press **Send to AI** to get the next versi

on. Show handled comments to see
the AI's reply on each one.
5. Press **Edit** on the latest version

to change text and formatting, then
**Save as new version**.

Start a new session for each document: a long session carries a lot of
context into every revision.
### Updates

On dsh 0.2.2 or later, when ultra-documents was installed from npm, the
document bar shows an **Upda

te to vX** button once a newer version is
published. Click it, then click **Confirm** within five se

conds; dsh's plugin
manager installs the new version and puts the old one back if that fails.
There

is no pop-up, and nothing shows when you are up to date, on an older
dsh, or on a GitHub or local in

stall. The check runs at most once every six
hours.
## How it works
| Piece | What it does |
| Agent tools | `ultra_documents_create`, `ultra_documents_revise`, `ultra_documents_comments`, `ult

ra_documents_list` |
| Skill | `ultra-documents`: when to use the tools and how to write the HTML (v

oice, visuals, styles, slides) |
| Sidebar renderer | Claims `*.ultra.html` files; renders the versi
on in an isolated sandbox with comment highlights, a comment panel, a version picker, direct editing

and full screen |
| Storage | `<workspace>/.ultra-documents/<slug>/` — `v1.ultra.html`, `v2.ultra.h
tml`, …, `doc.json`, `comments.json`; the directory is git-ignored |

Documents run in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` without same-origin
access: their scripts can
not reach the dsh page, its cookies or your files.
See docs/DESIGN.md for the design.
## Permissions and risks

- **Files:** writes only inside `<workspace>/.ultra-documents/`. The host side
writes with Node `fs`

and refuses any path that resolves outside the
workspace, including through symlinks. Drafts are re

ad only from regular
files inside the workspace.
- **What it adds to dsh:** four agent tools, one sk

ill, one slash command
(`/ultra-documents`, used by the sidebar to save comments and edits) and a
si

debar renderer for `*.ultra.html` files.
- **Network and external services:** the plugin itself make

s no network
requests and uses no external service. For the update check it asks dsh's
plugin manage

r, which looks up the `ultra-documents` package on your
configured npm registry (`pnpm view`) at mos

t once every six hours; nothing
about your documents is sent. A document the agent writes may load f

onts or
libraries from a CDN when it is displayed.
- **Model usage:** creating a document and Send t

o AI use your configured
model and its tokens. Comments and direct edits do not.
- **Document script

s:** run in a sandboxed iframe with no access to the dsh
page, its cookies or your files; they can o

nly open a link when you click
it.
## Known limitations

- Documents that run their own scripts can be commented on but not edited
directly.
- A session open

in two dsh processes at once (say the desktop app and
`dsh web`) is write-locked by one of them; sa

ving comments or edits from the
other fails.
- Each comment action shows a one-line "ultra-documents

" command card in the
chat. It never reaches the model.
- The sidebar polls for changes every 3 seco

nds, and a document opened before
a light/dark theme switch keeps its old theme until it is reopened

.
- Local filesystem only; Sessions on a remote filesystem are not supported.
- dsh is a release can
didate. Tested on 0.2.1-rc.3 and 0.2.2-rc.1.
